beats.text: For thousands of years, open water was a wall.
The oldest boat ever found is a dugout canoe, a hollowed log, about ten thousand years old.
Egyptians added sails, and let the wind do the work.
By the 1500s, giant galleons with many masts crossed entire oceans.
In 1807, Robert Fulton's steamboat didn't need wind at all.
Steel hulls and powerful engines soon made ships bigger than ever.
In 1956, the first container ship sailed, and shipping changed forever.
Today, the biggest ships carry over twenty thousand containers at once.
Follow to see how everything evolved.
